question: Which mask must nurses wear during procedures that generate aerosols on COVID-19 patients?

options.A: Plastic face shield alone
options.B: Cloth face covering
options.C: Standard paper surgical mask
options.D: N95 respirator

explanation: Procedures that kick tiny droplets into the air require a tight-fitting N95 mask to keep you safe. Safety first in nursing! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h7)

question: What should the nurse do before bringing a meal tray to a patient who needs feeding help?

options.A: Restrict all fluids until the meal is finished
options.B: Clear the bedside table and clean your hands
options.C: Give a sleeping pill to calm them down
options.D: Insist that family members feed every meal

explanation: Spot on! Basic hygiene and a clean, clutter-free space make mealtime safe and much more inviting. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h4)

question: Which detail must be included in the nursing documentation after a patient dies?

options.A: The financial status of the patient's family
options.B: The exact time death was pronounced
options.C: The names of all nurses working on the next shift
options.D: The exact cause of the underlying disease

explanation: The exact time of death pronouncement by the doctor is a legal requirement that must be documented in the nursing notes. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h6)

question: When the sympathetic nervous system kicks in during stress, what happens to your digestion?

options.A: It has no effect on the gut
options.B: It increases gastric acid output
options.C: It stimulates pancreatic enzyme release
options.D: It decreases digestive secretions

explanation: Think of the 'fight or flight' response—your body focuses on survival, not digesting food, so digestive secretions slow right down. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which of these side-to-side measurements is the wider one across a baby's skull?

options.A: The biparietal diameter
options.B: The bitemporal diameter
options.C: Neither is used in obstetrics
options.D: Both measure exactly the same

explanation: The biparietal diameter stretches across the widest part of the parietal bones, making it broader than the bitemporal measurement across the temples. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h4)

question: An employer demands to see the full medical diagnosis and lab results of a worker who visited your clinic. What are you ethically allowed to share?

options.A: The complete confidential medical history and psychiatric notes
options.B: Only the worker's fitness-for-work status and necessary job accommodations
options.C: No information whatsoever, ever
options.D: Detailed lab test values and family health records

explanation: You nailed it! To keep trust and protect privacy, you only tell the boss if the worker is fit for duty or needs special adjustments—keep the private diagnosis to yourself. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h8)

question: A newly admitted patient gets dizzy from medications and has a history of stumbling. What should you do first?

options.A: Keep the patient strictly confined to a wheelchair
options.B: Restrict all fluid intake to prevent bathroom trips
options.C: Order physical therapy to cure the dizziness immediately
options.D: Implement a targeted fall prevention care plan

explanation: Well done! Spotting risk factors early means you can put safety measures in place before the patient takes a tumble. [learn more](GST319_U4_T7#GST319_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended strategy for preventing harm from gishiri cuts?

options.A: Providing emergency obstetric services
options.B: Expanding access to skilled antenatal care
options.C: Community health education on pelvic anatomy
options.D: Training traditional birth attendants to perform safer cuts

explanation: The goal is to stop the practice entirely rather than make cutting safer, as the procedure itself lacks any medical validity. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h7)

question: Why should health workers turn complex data into simple instructions during an emergency?

options.A: To make the government reports look shorter and cleaner
options.B: Ordinary citizens need clear actions they can easily apply during emergencies
options.C: So that international media organizations can broadcast it faster
options.D: Because the public refuses to read scientific articles

explanation: You got it! When instructions are simple and direct, people can follow them quickly without confusion while under stress. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h1)

question: What do we call a child who is academically gifted but also has a learning disability?

options.A: Twice-exceptional
options.B: Developmentally delayed
options.C: Behaviorally challenged
options.D: Asynchronously balanced

explanation: Great job! 'Twice-exceptional' means the child is exceptional in two ways: they have high intellectual potential alongside a specific learning challenge. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T1#GNS225_U5_T1_h2)

question: A patient using axillary crutches complains of numbness and tingling in their fingers. What instruction should the nurse provide?

options.A: Switch immediately to using a standard four-wheeled walker
options.B: Adjust the crutches so they fit higher up in the armpit
options.C: Lean your upper body forward to relieve hand pressure
options.D: Support your body weight on your hands, not your armpits

explanation: Resting body weight on the armpits compresses nerves and blood vessels, leading to nerve damage and tingling; weight must go through the hand grips. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h4)

question: A patient with an unstable airway arrives at the emergency department at the same time as a patient with a sprained ankle. Who should be prioritized?

options.A: The patient with the unstable airway
options.B: The patient with the sprained ankle
options.C: Whichever patient has valid health insurance
options.D: Whoever arrived through the front doors first

explanation: Airway compromise is an immediate threat to life, placing that patient at the highest level of triage urgency. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h1)

question: What common home habit frequently leads to accidental drug poisoning in communities?

options.A: Drinking adequate amounts of clean water daily
options.B: Taking prescribed drugs strictly according to the label
options.C: Sharing prescription medicines and improper home storage
options.D: Storing medications inside a locked refrigerator

explanation: Leaving leftover drugs where kids can reach them—or passing your meds to a friend—is a major recipe for accidental poisoning at home. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T9#GNS125_U2_T9_h8)

question: What is the very next thing you must do after the AED delivers a shock?

options.A: Check the carotid pulse for at least one full minute
options.B: Turn the machine off and wait for the ambulance crew
options.C: Remove the sticky pads and wipe the skin with alcohol
options.D: Resume chest compressions and CPR for two minutes

explanation: Right after a shock, don't wait—jump right back into CPR starting with chest compressions to keep blood moving! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT something a food safety supervisor needs to check?

options.A: Observing proper handwashing compliance
options.B: Monitoring refrigerator and freezer temperatures
options.C: Checking employee credit history records
options.D: Inspecting the safe storage of raw and cooked food

explanation: An employee's financial history has nothing to do with food safety! Inspections focus purely on hygiene and temperature control. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h5)

question: A nurse uses a pain scale that somehow measures patient hunger instead of pain. Which quality is this tool lacking?

options.A: Reliability
options.B: Length
options.C: Practicality
options.D: Validity

explanation: When an instrument measures the wrong concept, it lacks validity because it is not capturing what it claims to measure. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h2)

question: A patient in skin traction complains of severe leg spasms, and the nurse sees the rope is caught on the pulley wheel. What is the best first step?

options.A: Realign the rope smoothly into the center of the pulley groove
options.B: Cut the traction tape immediately to release all skin pressure
options.C: Administer a stronger pain pill and wait for relief
options.D: Raise the head of the bed high

explanation: You've got this! When a rope slips, the weights stop pulling correctly, which causes muscle spasms. Just pop the rope back into the groove to fix the tension right away. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the main goal when a ward manager designs a proper duty roster?

options.A: Matching patient care needs with the right staff mix and shifts
options.B: Ensuring every nurse works only night shifts permanently
options.C: Allowing senior staff to avoid working weekends entirely
options.D: Reducing the total number of nurses employed in the hospital

explanation: A good roster is like a puzzle piece: it matches the skills and numbers of available nurses directly with how sick the patients are. [learn more](GST321_U1_T9#GST321_U1_T9_h7)

question: A nursing unit spends much more money on medical supplies this month than the budget allowed. How is this situation called?

options.A: A favorable variance
options.B: An unfavorable variance
options.C: A capital surplus
options.D: A balanced revenue stream

explanation: When your expenses go higher than your budgeted plan, it's called an unfavorable variance and means you need to recheck your spending. [learn more](GST321_U1_T23#GST321_U1_T23_h5)

question: What is the proper term for healthcare services given to a woman during pregnancy?

options.A: Paediatric surveillance
options.B: Postpartum recovery
options.C: Antenatal care
options.D: Gynecological screening

explanation: Antenatal care (ANC) is simply the medical supervision and support given to an expectant mother throughout her pregnancy. You've got this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T49#GNS214_U1_T49_h1)

question: Why can repeated or chronic ovarian infections lead to long-term fertility problems?

options.A: White blood cells destroy all female hormones
options.B: The uterus shrinks to prevent egg implantation
options.C: Scar tissue develops during healing, blocking pelvic structures
options.D: The ovaries permanently stop making estrogen

explanation: Just like a skin wound leaves a scar, healing reproductive tissue can form adhesions and scar tissue that block the tubes and trap the ovaries, making pregnancy difficult. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T31#GNS216_U5_T31_h3)

question: Why must a nurse always wear gloves when applying topical medications to a patient?

options.A: To warm up the cream before it makes direct contact with the patient's body
options.B: To prevent the patient's natural skin bacteria from contaminating the medication tube
options.C: To keep the patient's room environment completely sterile during the procedure
options.D: To protect the nurse from accidentally absorbing the medication through their own skin

explanation: Many topical drugs are potent and can easily pass through the nurse's fingertips into their own bloodstream if gloves are omitted. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h6)

question: Which situation best demonstrates a violation of a client's basic healthcare rights?

options.A: A doctor explains the potential side effects of a prescribed medication
options.B: A nurse assists a recovering client with taking a morning bath
options.C: A nurse discusses a patient's private diagnosis openly in a crowded hallway
options.D: A client asks questions about the hospital meal schedule before eating

explanation: Sharing private health information publicly violates the patient's right to confidentiality and respectful treatment. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h1)

question: What are the classic signs that a patient has developed a post-abortion pelvic infection?

options.A: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge and fever
options.B: Clear, watery discharge lasting several days
options.C: Sudden painless swelling of the lower limbs
options.D: High blood pressure and severe throbbing headache

explanation: Spot on! Bad-smelling discharge and fever are major warning signs that bacteria have entered the uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h5)

question: Which gland releases a hormone to raise blood calcium when it drops too low?

options.A: Parathyroid gland
options.B: Thyroid gland
options.C: Adrenal gland
options.D: Pancreas

explanation: Spot on! The tiny parathyroid glands step in with parathyroid hormone to pull calcium back into the blood when levels fall. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T1#GNS211_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR)?

options.A: Empowering local communities to support and integrate children with disabilities
options.B: Eliminating the need for any hospital visits
options.C: Training only foreign doctors in local customs
options.D: Relocating all special children to central urban orphanages

explanation: CBR is all about using local resources and community spirit to ensure children with disabilities thrive right where they live. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T7#GNS225_U5_T7_h4)

question: Why shouldn't a nurse just hand out a generic diet pamphlet and call it a day?

options.A: Patients refuse to read any written information while admitted
options.B: Dietitians forbid nurses from using printed instructional materials
options.C: Hospital pamphlets are always outdated and medically incorrect
options.D: Patients have unique cultural, financial, and physical backgrounds

explanation: Great thinking! No two patients are the same. Good nursing care means tailoring advice to fit what the patient actually eats, loves, and can afford. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h1)

question: A nurse manager holds a staff meeting to ask everyone for ideas on how to fix the weekend scheduling roster. What leadership style is being used?

options.A: Coercive
options.B: Democratic
options.C: Laissez-faire
options.D: Autocratic

explanation: Asking the team for input and involving them in decisions is the hallmark of democratic leadership. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h5)

question: Which agency plays a massive role in rolling out national immunization campaigns down to local communities?

options.A: Federal Inland Revenue Service
options.B: National Primary Health Care Development Agency
options.C: Nigerian Tourism Development Corporation
options.D: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing

explanation: You nailed it! The NPHCDA is the key driver behind primary healthcare support and nationwide vaccination drives in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T26#GNS225_U5_T26_h5)

question: When we talk about resource mobilization for a project, what does it include besides money?

options.A: Gathering medical supplies, outreach spaces, and local volunteers
options.B: Closing down existing health posts to save money
options.C: Reducing the number of staff required to run the clinic
options.D: Waiting for international organizations to supply all equipment

explanation: Resources aren't just cash in hand. They include everything from a good venue for outreach to willing volunteers and basic supplies. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h3)

question: What is the best first step when a patient suddenly has a bloody nose?

options.A: Instruct the client to blow the nose hard to clear out clots
options.B: Pack both nasal cavities tightly with dry gauze strips immediately
options.C: Place the client flat on their back and tilt the head backward
options.D: Have the client sit upright and lean forward while pinching the soft nose

explanation: You nailed it! Leaning forward keeps blood out of the throat, and pinching the soft part of the nose puts direct pressure right where it's bleeding. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why must you be careful of the chemical reaction when mixing Plaster of Paris with water?

options.A: It generates heat as it sets and hardens
options.B: It produces toxic fumes during mixing
options.C: It expands to double its original size
options.D: It absorbs ambient room moisture rapidly

explanation: The setting process is exothermic, meaning it gives off heat. You want to keep this in mind so it doesn't cause skin discomfort or burns! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h1)

question: How do nurses directly help keep drugs safe after they are already released to the public?

options.A: By manufacturing safer alternative medications in hospital pharmacies
options.B: By setting the official market price for all new pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: By reporting unexpected and unusual drug reactions to authorities
options.D: By conducting clinical trials on animals in hospital laboratories

explanation: Nurses are at the bedside every day, making you the crucial eyes and ears for reporting strange side effects and protecting the public! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h7)

question: Why is routine urinalysis important during pregnancy checkups?

options.A: It checks for protein and sugar, which show kidney stress or diabetes
options.B: It measures the heartbeat of the unborn baby
options.C: It tells the nurse the exact weight of the placenta
options.D: It proves whether the mother is eating enough vegetables

explanation: Protein in urine can point to pre-eclampsia, while sugar can point to diabetes, both needing close management. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h5)

question: Why might a doctor order a CT scan after a biopsy confirms vulval cancer?

options.A: To measure the exact resting heart rate of the patient
options.B: To find out if the patient has a history of skin allergies
options.C: To check if the cancer has spread to lymph nodes or other organs
options.D: To determine if the patient has a secondary urinary tract infection

explanation: Well done! Imaging tests help us stage the cancer by showing if abnormal cells have travelled to nearby lymph nodes or further away. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h5)

question: What is the medical term for the hard bumps of urate crystals that form under the skin in long-standing gout?

options.A: Tophi
options.B: Vesicle
options.C: Nodule
options.D: Pannus

explanation: Tophi are those visible lumps of uric acid crystals that can pop up under the skin or around joints when gout isn't well controlled over time. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T11#GNS222_U1_T11_h3)

question: What often happens to ongoing health programs in Nigeria when a new political administration takes over?

options.A: Complete elimination of the federal ministry of health
options.B: Automatic privatization of all public teaching hospitals
options.C: Immediate reduction of nurse salaries nationwide
options.D: Disruption of ongoing health projects due to changing agendas

explanation: Spot on! New leaders often drop old projects to focus on their own fresh ideas, which can sadly slow down long-term progress in the health sector. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h2)

question: A patient on continuous tube feeding has a red, sore spot right on the edge of their nostril. What should you do?

options.A: Clean the skin, apply a protective cream, and tape the tube to a slightly different spot
options.B: Put thick gauze padding under the tube
options.C: Leave the tape loose so the tube rubs freely
options.D: Pull the tube out permanently and stop feeding

explanation: Protecting the skin and shifting the pressure point gives the sore spot a chance to heal while keeping the patient fed. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of qualitative data analysis in healthcare research?

options.A: Measuring the exact blood pressure drop after medication
options.B: Counting how many hospital beds are filled each night
options.C: Calculating exact drug dosages and patient body weights
options.D: Exploring human experiences, feelings, and recurring themes

explanation: Qualitative research focuses on understanding the subjective experiences and perspectives of participants rather than measuring quantities. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common trigger for a sickle cell pain crisis?

options.A: Dehydration from drinking too little water
options.B: An underlying viral or bacterial infection
options.C: Exposure to sudden cold weather environments
options.D: Eating a diet high in green leafy vegetables

explanation: Green leafy vegetables are healthy and safe! Infections, cold weather, and not drinking enough water are the real troublemakers that trigger a painful crisis. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T7#GNS311_U2_T7_h7)

question: What is the difference between anonymity and confidentiality?

options.A: Anonymity means no one can link data to a name; confidentiality keeps known identities secret
options.B: Anonymity is optional in nursing research; confidentiality is strictly mandatory
options.C: Anonymity applies only to secondary data; confidentiality applies to primary data
options.D: There is no difference between the two terms in clinical research studies

explanation: Anonymity means nobody (not even the researcher) knows whose data is whose. Confidentiality means you know who they are, but you keep their identity locked away safe. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h6)

question: Why is it important for nurses to know the physical signs of grief?

options.A: To prevent mistaking normal grief reactions for physical illness
options.B: To stop patients from feeling any physical pain
options.C: To prove that grief is purely a physical disease
options.D: To prescribe strong antibiotics for chest tightness

explanation: Spot on! Recognizing that things like stomach ache or trouble sleeping are normal grief signs stops unnecessary medical tests and reassures the patient. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T10#GNS321_U4_T10_h4)

question: A community nurse is preparing to measure a toddler's MUAC. Where on the arm should the tape be placed to find the correct midpoint?

options.A: At the thickest part of the bicep muscle
options.B: Right below the armpit crease
options.C: Directly over the middle of the forearm
options.D: Between the shoulder tip and the elbow tip

explanation: You've got this! To get an accurate MUAC, always locate the exact midpoint between the shoulder (acromion) and the elbow (olecranon). [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h5)

question: What does drug over-prescription mean in clinical practice?

options.A: Storing too many pharmaceutical products in the hospital pharmacy
options.B: Giving medicines that are unnecessary or in too high a dose
options.C: Ordering only herbal remedies instead of orthodox drugs
options.D: Failing to give any medication to a critically ill patient

explanation: Over-prescription happens when patients receive drugs they do not need or take excessive quantities that can harm them. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h1)

question: A patient is anxious and has a rapid heart rate before surgery. Which nursing action is best to help calm them?

options.A: Advise the patient to ignore the upcoming surgery entirely
options.B: Leave the patient alone in a brightly lit room to rest
options.C: Guide the patient through slow deep breathing exercises
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink several cups of strong coffee

explanation: Taking slow, deep breaths is a simple, powerful way to quiet the fight-or-flight response, slow down a racing heart, and ease pre-surgery nerves. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T8#GNS123_U1_T8_h7)

question: What is the best way to ask a patient about suspected abuse during a nursing assessment?

options.A: Using private, non-judgmental, and direct questions
options.B: Warning the patient about the legal consequences of lying
options.C: Waiting until the patient brings up the topic spontaneously
options.D: Asking in front of family members to get confirmation

explanation: You've got this! A private, gentle, and non-blaming approach makes patients feel safe enough to open up. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T8#GNS312_U4_T8_h5)

question: What is the main use of a family planning client register in the clinic?

options.A: To record detailed client information and services given sequentially
options.B: To track daily weather patterns affecting clinic attendance
options.C: To advertise new contraceptive brands to visiting community members
options.D: To list the financial debts owed by the local health facility

explanation: Great thinking! The client register keeps a neat, step-by-step history of everyone who visits for family planning care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h2)

question: What is the main medical goal of giving a patient a sitz bath?

options.A: To lower a very high fever using freezing cold water
options.B: To increase joint flexibility in patients with severe arthritis
options.C: To reduce pain and swelling in the perineal and rectal area
options.D: To scrub off dead skin cells from the entire body surface

explanation: You've got this! A sitz bath focuses warm water right on the lower trunk to soothe discomfort from things like hemorrhoids or childbirth. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h2)

question: A patient in the emergency ward has a racing heart, high blood pressure, and extreme restlessness after taking a drug. What kind of drug is most likely behind this?

options.A: Barbiturates
options.B: Depressants
options.C: Cannabinoids
options.D: Stimulants

explanation: Spot on! Stimulants like cocaine or amphetamines rev up the nervous system, leading to high energy, fast heart rates, and agitation. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T5#GNS223_U6_T5_h3)

question: What is the main goal of doing a thoracentesis?

options.A: To clear mucus plugs from the main airways
options.B: To measure pressure inside the right atrium
options.C: To deliver medications directly into the lung tissue
options.D: To remove fluid or air from the pleural space

explanation: You've got this! A thoracentesis simply means putting a tiny needle into the chest cavity to drain out unwanted fluid or air that shouldn't be there. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h1)

question: What unit of measurement is commonly used to express dietary energy?

options.A: Centimeters
options.B: Kilocalories
options.C: Milliliters
options.D: Milligrams

explanation: Dietary energy is measured in kilocalories, which are commonly called calories on food labels and in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h1)

question: You want to build a good relationship with a family caring for an elderly relative at home. What is the best way to start?

options.A: Inform the family of all the household rules they are currently breaking
options.B: Avoid asking personal questions to maintain strict professional distance
options.C: Show sincere interest in the family's daily routines and overall well-being
options.D: Focus exclusively on checking the patient's medication chart immediately

explanation: Showing genuine care for their everyday life helps break the ice and builds a wonderful, trusting relationship beyond just the illness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h3)

question: What does motivation mean in a healthcare workplace?

options.A: The financial bonus given for working extra weekend shifts
options.B: The inner drive that directs behavior toward achieving specific goals
options.C: The mandatory number of clinical hours a nurse works each week
options.D: The strict enforcement of hospital policies by upper management

explanation: Motivation is simply that inner push or enthusiasm that keeps you going toward a goal. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U1_T18#GST321_U1_T18_h1)

question: After teaching an insulin-dependent diabetic client how to inject medication at home, what must the nurse document?

options.A: The specific teaching content, the method used, and the client's return demonstration
options.B: Only the date and time of the home visit without mentioning the teaching
options.C: That the client bought an expensive refrigerator for storing the insulin
options.D: That teaching is unnecessary because the client is educated

explanation: Documenting education requires proof of what was taught and how the client showed they understood it. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why is it better to test changes using small PDSA cycles instead of a massive hospital-wide overhaul?

options.A: It guarantees that every single change attempted will be successful on the first try.
options.B: It allows staff to test ideas safely, learn quickly, and minimize risk before wide adoption.
options.C: It prevents nurses from having to participate in unit meetings.
options.D: It completely eliminates the need to collect any patient data.

explanation: Smart thinking! Testing on a small scale keeps patients safe and lets you iron out any wrinkles without turning the whole hospital upside down. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h4)

question: Where is the best place to keep your sharps disposal box during an injection?

options.A: In the nurse's station for later
options.B: Locked in a store room down the hall
options.C: On the floor right under the patient's bed
options.D: Right within arm's reach of your workspace

explanation: Keep your safety box close! Walking around with an open, used needle just asks for an accidental poke. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of accident prevention in nursing care?

options.A: Strict bedrest enforcement
options.B: Expensive home renovations
options.C: Proactive risk identification
options.D: Punishing careless behaviors

explanation: Nurses focus heavily on finding and fixing hazards before an actual injury happens to the patient. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h1)

question: What usually happens to your search precision when you broaden your search terms to increase recall?

options.A: Precision increases because the computer works twice as fast
options.B: Precision drops to zero because the system crashes immediately
options.C: Precision stays exactly the same regardless of search terms
options.D: Precision decreases because more irrelevant results get pulled in

explanation: There is a classic inverse relationship between precision and recall; casting a wider net brings in more noise along with the good articles. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which of the following is a simple, effective home method to make unsafe drinking water safer?

options.A: Adding heavy machine oil to the bucket
options.B: Boiling the water thoroughly
options.C: Leaving the water uncovered in the sun
options.D: Stirring the water with a dirty stick

explanation: Boiling kills harmful bacteria, viruses, and parasites present in untreated water sources. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h4)

question: What does a psychoactive substance mainly do to the human body?

options.A: It permanently repairs damaged nerve tissues
options.B: It alters brain function and mental state

question: Why don't standard painkillers like ibuprofen work well for severe nerve pain?

question: Why must a nurse view pharmacotherapy as a balance between benefits and risks?

options.A: Therapeutic effects only occur when toxic reactions are actively triggered
options.B: Patients will refuse treatment if they know about any potential side effects
options.C: Every medication carries some level of inherent hazard alongside its healing properties
options.D: Hospital policies require reporting all minor medication side effects daily

explanation: All drugs have the potential to cause harm, so nurses must weigh therapeutic gains against possible toxic effects. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is the role of Montgomery tubercles (those tiny bumps on the areola) during pregnancy and breastfeeding?

options.A: They control the blood flow through the lactiferous sinuses
options.B: They anchor the suspensory ligaments to the chest wall
options.C: They secrete a lubricating substance to protect the nipple
options.D: They produce human placental lactogen to support the fetus

explanation: Montgomery glands make a natural, oily lotion that keeps the skin of the nipple and areola soft and protected from cracking. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T10#GNS121_U7_T10_h3)

question: What defines a pre-testicular cause of male infertility?

options.A: A physical blockage within the epididymis preventing sperm release
options.B: A genetic mutation residing directly on the chromosomes inside the sperm
options.C: A hormonal or systemic problem outside the testes that disrupts sperm production
options.D: An infection of the prostate gland that damages the seminal fluid

explanation: Pre-testicular issues originate in the brain or endocrine system before the signal ever reaches the testicles. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h2)

question: Which fluid fills the large cavity behind the lens to keep the retina in place?

options.A: Aqueous humor
options.B: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: Synovial fluid
options.D: Vitreous humor

explanation: Vitreous humor is a thick gel that fills the posterior segment and keeps the eyeball from collapsing. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the main job of the Olfactory nerve (Cranial Nerve I)?

options.A: Smell
options.B: Hearing
options.C: Vision
options.D: Taste

explanation: Spot on! Cranial Nerve I is our olfactory nerve, carrying messages about different smells from our nose up to the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T15#GNS211_U3_T15_h2)

question: Which strategy is most effective when educating rural community members about pregnancy danger signs?

options.A: Using simple local dialects and relatable community gathering spaces
options.B: Hosting lectures exclusively in urban tertiary teaching hospitals
options.C: Requiring written exams before women can attend antenatal care
options.D: Distributing dense medical journals written in advanced technical terms

explanation: Effective community health education meets people where they are, using familiar language and local venues like markets or places of worship. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h5)

question: A patient has an infected wound on their right hand and notices tender lumps in their right armpit. What does this mean?

options.A: The patient has a primary blood disorder originating in the spleen
options.B: The patient is experiencing normal side effects of red blood cell breakdown
options.C: Bacteria from the hand wound are traveling through lymph vessels to the axillary nodes
options.D: Blockage of the thoracic duct has caused fluid backup in the upper extremity

explanation: Lymph drains from specific regions of the body to nearby nodes. An infection in the hand travels up the arm vessels, causing the armpit (axillary) nodes to trap the germs and swell up. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h5)

question: Why do tablets or injections (systemic drugs) often struggle to treat eye problems effectively?

options.A: Blood vessels in the eye destroy active ingredients
options.B: Unique barriers like the cornea block them from getting inside
options.C: Systemic drugs cannot dissolve in body fluids
options.D: The liver breaks down all eye medications too quickly

explanation: Think of the eye as a well-guarded fort! Natural barriers like the cornea make it hard for drugs travelling through your bloodstream to get inside the eye in strong enough amounts. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h1)

question: What important skill do sperm cells pick up while chilling in the epididymis?

options.A: They mix with acidic prostate fluid
options.B: They multiply rapidly through mitosis
options.C: They gain the ability to swim
options.D: They lose their tails completely

explanation: Think of the epididymis as a training ground where immature sperm finally develop motility so they can swim forward. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the term for weak, lazy uterine contractions that fail to open the cervix?

options.A: Occiput posterior
options.B: Cephalopelvic disproportion
options.C: Uterine inertia
options.D: Uterine hyperstimulation

explanation: Spot on! 'Inertia' means lack of movement or energy. The uterus is simply too tired or weak to push the process along. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T003#GNS226_U3_T003_h4)

question: Which planning level gives a broad, long-term picture of what an organization wants to achieve?

options.A: A task
options.B: A routine
options.C: A goal
options.D: An objective

explanation: Goals are the big picture—the ultimate vision of where the facility wants to be in the long run. [learn more](GST321_U2_T1#GST321_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in a project?

options.A: Monitoring happens after the project ends, while evaluation happens before it starts.
options.B: Monitoring deals with money, while evaluation deals strictly with medicines.
options.C: Monitoring is done by the community, while evaluation is done by politicians.
options.D: Monitoring tracks activities during implementation, while evaluation measures final impact.

explanation: Spot on! Monitoring is what you do while the work is going on, while evaluation checks the final results after everything is done. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main job of hCG (the pregnancy hormone) in the early weeks?

options.A: To signal the corpus luteum to keep making progesterone
options.B: To trigger the immediate production of mature breast milk
options.C: To lower maternal blood pressure to prevent hypertension
options.D: To soften the pelvic ligaments for upcoming delivery

explanation: Spot on! hCG tells the body's temporary structure (the corpus luteum) to stay put and keep pumping out progesterone to keep the pregnancy safe. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T14#GNS121_U5_T14_h2)

question: What is a great lifestyle step to help restore regular ovulation in a patient with PCOS and insulin resistance?

options.A: Avoiding all forms of dietary protein
options.B: Strict bed rest for several weeks
options.C: Complete elimination of dietary water
options.D: Weight management and regular exercise

explanation: Lifestyle is powerful medicine! Getting regular exercise and managing weight helps the body handle insulin better, which naturally helps balance hormones and restore ovulation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary physiological mechanism that causes pressure injuries to form over bony prominences?

options.A: Excessive surface sweat softens the outer skin layer until it tears
options.B: Prolonged pressure cuts off capillary blood flow, causing tissue ischemia
options.C: Bacterial growth multiplies rapidly inside healthy sweat glands
options.D: The body's immune system attacks normal skin cells by mistake

explanation: When external pressure exceeds normal capillary pressure, blood flow stops, starving the tissues of oxygen and nutrients and causing cell death. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h7)

question: The main economic driver for forced marriage in impoverished households is:

options.A: Funding expensive higher education for male siblings
options.B: Gaining immediate access to high-paying government jobs
options.C: Reducing household financial burdens and securing bride wealth
options.D: Paying off international business loans with banks

explanation: Poverty pushes some families to marry off young dependents to cut down expenses and receive financial gains like bride price. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h2)

question: What system do water-soluble hormones use to pass along messages inside a cell?

options.A: Direct nuclear transcription
options.B: Intracellular cholesterol
options.C: Second messenger systems
options.D: Direct DNA replication

explanation: Since water-soluble hormones can't enter the cell themselves, they drop their message off at the surface, triggering a 'second messenger' inside the cell to carry out the orders. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T10#GNS211_U1_T10_h7)

question: What is the main job of carbohydrates in our bodies?

options.A: Producing protective antibodies for immunity
options.B: Transporting fat-soluble vitamins in blood
options.C: Providing the main source of daily energy
options.D: Repairing damaged muscle tissues and bones

explanation: You got it! Carbs break down into glucose, which is your brain's and muscles' favorite and most efficient fuel for the day. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h2)

question: A mother cannot afford the expensive imported supplements recommended for her underweight toddler. As her nurse, what should you do?

options.A: Tell her that nutrition counseling is no longer necessary if she cannot afford items
options.B: Help the mother adapt affordable, locally available foods to enrich the child's diet
options.C: Advise her to stop feeding the child solid foods until financial aid arrives
options.D: Insist that she buy the expensive supplements regardless of her financial situation

explanation: Real nursing meets people where they are. Great health education uses accessible, local market foods to make nutritious meals practical for every family. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h7)

question: What should you do if your final results turn out different from your original guess (hypothesis)?

options.A: Delete the unexpected data points from the final report
options.B: Report the actual findings honestly and objectively
options.C: Hide the entire study so nobody sees the mistake
options.D: Change the original hypothesis to match the new data

explanation: Integrity is key in nursing research. Always report what the data actually says, even if it surprises you! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h6)

question: What kind of information does qualitative research usually collect?

options.A: Machine-recorded heart monitor printouts
options.B: Exact laboratory blood test numbers
options.C: Statistical charts of hospital bed capacity
options.D: Words, interviews, and personal experiences

explanation: Spot on! Qualitative research explores human feelings and experiences by collecting descriptive text through interviews and observation. Think 'qual' for quality and stories! [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which type of incontinence happens when a person leaks urine while coughing, sneezing, or lifting heavy objects?

options.A: Stress urinary incontinence
options.B: Functional urinary incontinence
options.C: Urge urinary incontinence
options.D: Overflow urinary incontinence

explanation: Stress incontinence is triggered by physical movements that suddenly push down on the bladder when pelvic support is weak. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h3)

question: A patient is going home with a new antibiotic prescription. What crucial tip must you give them?

options.A: Stop taking the capsules the moment your fever breaks
options.B: Share leftover tablets with family members who catch the same infection
options.C: Complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms disappear early
options.D: Store all antibiotic bottles in the direct sunlight on your veranda

explanation: Remind patients to finish their full dose! Stopping early can cause the infection to bounce back stronger and cause drug resistance. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T2#GNS125_U3_T2_h6)

question: A patient is dealing with loneliness and money troubles after losing their partner. What do these life events represent?

options.A: Genetic and chromosomal mutations
options.B: Environmental and situational stressors
options.C: Primary endocrine abnormalities
options.D: Congenital brain structural defects

explanation: You nailed it! Things happening in a person's surroundings—like loss, isolation, or financial stress—are situational triggers that can spark depression. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T2#GNS324_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is a major root cause of unwanted pregnancies that lead to unsafe abortions?

options.A: Universal access to emergency birth control pills
options.B: Unmet needs and lack of access to modern contraceptives
options.C: Mandatory sex education classes in all primary schools
options.D: Excessive availability of free family planning clinics

explanation: When people cannot get or afford reliable birth control, unplanned pregnancies happen more often. Patient education is our best tool here! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h3)

question: Which pH test result tells you that the nasogastric tube is successfully resting in the stomach?

options.A: A high reading of 9.0
options.B: An alkaline reading of 8.5
options.C: A reading of 4.0
options.D: A neutral reading of 7.0

explanation: Stomach contents are acidic, so a low pH (like 4.0 or lower) is a strong sign that your tube is in the right place. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h5)

question: In type 1 diabetes, which part of the body does the immune system mistakenly attack?

options.A: The lining of the small intestine
options.B: Insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas
options.C: The protective sheaths around nerves
options.D: The membranes lining major joints

explanation: Type 1 diabetes is a classic autoimmune condition where the body turns on its own pancreas, destroying the beta cells that make insulin. Brilliant connection to remember! [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h3)

question: What causes re-expansion pulmonary edema during chest fluid drainage?

options.A: Removing a large volume of fluid too quickly
options.B: Using a needle that is too wide for the intercostal space
options.C: Failing to give the patient local anesthetic before starting
options.D: Positioning the patient on the wrong side afterward

explanation: You've got this! Draining too much fluid too fast places sudden stress on the lung blood vessels, causing fluid to seep into the tiny air sacs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h6)

question: Where is the main control center or 'thermostat' for human body temperature located?

options.A: The spinal cord
options.B: The medulla oblongata
options.C: The hypothalamus
options.D: The cerebellum

explanation: Well done! The hypothalamus in the brain acts as our internal thermostat, checking our temperature and making adjustments. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h3)

question: When a registered nurse delegates a task to a junior worker, what happens to the ultimate accountability for that patient's care?

options.A: It transfers completely to the healthcare worker who performs the task
options.B: It remains with the registered nurse who delegated the task
options.C: It is shared equally between the hospital management and the worker
options.D: It dissolves once the task is completed and documented

explanation: Remember this golden nursing rule: you can delegate tasks, but the ultimate accountability for patient care always stays with the Registered Nurse! [learn more](GST321_U1_T16#GST321_U1_T16_h4)

question: What must a nurse do immediately after wiping a medication vial rubber top with an alcohol swab?

options.A: Allow the alcohol to dry completely before piercing
options.B: Blow on the rubber top to dry it fast
options.C: Insert the needle immediately while it is wet
options.D: Rinse the top with sterile tap water

explanation: Giving the alcohol time to air dry ensures proper disinfection of the rubber stopper surface. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why should nurses involve traditional and religious leaders when starting a new community health project?

options.A: They provide free medical supplies to the clinic
options.B: Their approval builds trust and community acceptance
options.C: They are trained to audit hospital financial records
options.D: They write all official government health policies

explanation: Community leaders hold great influence. When they support a health initiative, the people are much more willing to listen and participate. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is a key professional duty of every nurse when it comes to injection safety?

options.A: Hiding unsafe practices to protect the hospital's image
options.B: Refusing unsafe practices and speaking up for proper supplies
options.C: Reusing needles when the hospital budget is tight
options.D: Leaving all injections to untrained volunteers

explanation: As a nurse, your primary loyalty is to safety. You have an ethical duty to speak up against dangerous shortcuts and shortages. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h8)

question: Where are community health nurses most likely to meet families to talk about the value of school?

options.A: Inside high courtrooms during child custody legal proceedings
options.B: During parliamentary budget planning sessions in the capital city
options.C: During home visits, immunization clinics, and community meetings
options.D: At international nursing research conferences held overseas

explanation: Spot on! Routine outreach gives nurses a great chance to chat directly with parents right where they live and gather. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T47#GNS214_U1_T47_h4)

question: What is the main medication used to treat General Paralysis of the Insane?

options.A: Corticosteroid shots
options.B: Intravenous Penicillin G
options.C: Oral antiviral tablets
options.D: Insulin injections

explanation: Well done! High-dose intravenous penicillin G is our top weapon to clear the Treponema pallidum bacteria out of the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T1#GNS222_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which vaccine is routinely given during pregnancy to protect the newborn from a deadly infection?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid
options.B: Measles vaccine
options.C: Bacille Calmette-Guérin
options.D: Hepatitis A vaccine

explanation: Spot on! Tetanus toxoid is given to expectant mothers to protect their babies from neonatal tetanus. Great memory! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h3)

question: How does Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) differ from basic health education?

options.A: BCC focuses on active behavior change rather than just sharing information
options.B: Basic health education involves no communication at all
options.C: BCC is only used inside tertiary hospitals by doctors
options.D: Basic education is meant for children while BCC is for adults

explanation: Think of it this way: health education gives people the facts, but BCC goes a step further to help them actually overcome personal and social barriers to take action. You're building solid community nursing foundations! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h1)

question: Why are healthcare-associated infections a major concern in nursing?

options.A: They prolong hospital stays and increase patient suffering
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for antibiotics
options.C: They only affect nurses who fail to wear gloves
options.D: They are caused exclusively by patient diet changes

explanation: Infections acquired during healthcare delivery add heavy burdens to patients by worsening their health and lengthening their recovery time. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h1)

question: What is one of the biggest goals of home-based nursing care?

options.A: Reducing the need for any future medical checkups
options.B: Ensuring the patient moves permanently to a nursing home
options.C: Preventing unnecessary hospital readmissions
options.D: Eliminating the involvement of family members

explanation: Exactly! By managing health well at home, we keep patients comfortable and out of crowded hospital beds. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T1#GNS324_U1_T1_h3)

question: What tip should a nurse give a pregnant woman to help prevent severe morning nausea?

options.A: Drink a large glass of orange juice immediately upon waking up
options.B: Skip breakfast entirely until the afternoon hours arrive
options.C: Keep plain crackers near the bed and eat a small amount before getting up
options.D: Exercise vigorously for twenty minutes before eating breakfast

explanation: Nibbling a dry cracker before getting out of bed lifts morning blood sugar and settles an empty stomach. Classic nursing advice that really helps patients! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h8)

question: How do patriarchal community structures contribute to forced marriage?

options.A: By legally requiring women to register businesses in their husband's name
options.B: By forcing young men to marry older women for inheritance
options.C: By banning all forms of traditional marriage ceremonies entirely
options.D: By giving male family members total control over female relatives' lives

explanation: Patriarchal norms concentrate decision-making power in the hands of men, making it easier to override a woman's personal choice. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which of the following is a modifiable risk factor for hypertension?

options.A: Family genetic history
options.B: Chronological aging
options.C: Biological sex
options.D: High dietary salt intake

explanation: Modifiable risk factors are lifestyle habits or conditions that a person can change, such as reducing salt intake, unlike age or genetics. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h2)

question: When is the right time to start transmission-based precautions for a patient?

options.A: At the first sign of symptoms or upon suspicion of infection
options.B: After public health officers visit the ward
options.C: When the patient requests a private hospital room
options.D: Only after laboratory confirmation is fully finalized

explanation: Spot on! Waiting for lab results takes time, and germs don't wait. As soon as you suspect an infection, start precautions right away to keep everyone safe. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h1)

question: What do physical therapists mainly focus on during rehabilitation?

options.A: Fine motor coordination and cooking skills
options.B: Emotional coping and mental health support
options.C: Large muscle movements and lower body walking
options.D: Speech articulation and swallowing safety

explanation: Think of PTs as the experts on big movements! They focus on large muscles, balance, walking, and helping patients move around safely. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T3#GNS123_U6_T3_h4)

question: A patient has an injury affecting the clear gel that fills the main cavity behind the lens. What is this gel called?

options.A: The vitreous humor
options.B: The corneal stroma
options.C: The pupillary fluid
options.D: The aqueous humor

explanation: The vitreous humor is the jelly-like substance that gives the eyeball its stable shape behind the lens. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h2)

question: Why is talking about food such a powerful tool when nursing patients with chronic illnesses?

options.A: Dietary changes directly influence disease progression and symptoms
options.B: It cures genetic disorders before birth
options.C: It completely replaces the need for prescribed medications
options.D: It lowers the patient's hospital utility bills

explanation: You nailed it. For conditions like diabetes or heart disease, what the patient eats every day acts like medicine—or makes things worse. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h4)

question: Which of these is a common reason a patient with infective endocarditis might need surgical valve replacement?

options.A: Temporary joint pain in the lower extremities
options.B: Heart failure caused by severe valve damage
options.C: A slight elevation in white blood cell count
options.D: Mild fatigue during routine daily activities

explanation: When an infection destroys the heart valves so badly that the heart starts failing or fluid overloads the body, surgery becomes necessary to fix or replace the valve. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the main way the poliovirus spreads in a community?

options.A: Inhalation of respiratory droplets from sneezing
options.B: Direct skin contact with an infected skin rash
options.C: Vector-borne transmission via mosquito bites
options.D: Fecal-oral route through contaminated water or food

explanation: Spot on! Polio spreads mainly through the fecal-oral route, usually when people consume food or water contaminated with infected waste. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h3)

question: A patient taking daily prednisone reports sudden weight gain and swollen ankles. What is the best first nursing action?

options.A: Administer a stat dose of an oral antibiotic to prevent sepsis
options.B: Recommend doubling the daily sodium intake in the patient's diet
options.C: Instruct the patient to stop taking the prednisone immediately
options.D: Assess lung sounds and check blood pressure for fluid overload

explanation: Sudden weight gain and swollen ankles scream fluid retention! As a sharp nurse, your next step is to check how far that fluid has traveled by listening to lung sounds and checking blood pressure. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h6)

question: What must you always do right before an AED analyzes the heart rhythm or delivers a shock?

options.A: Check the patient's pupils with a penlight
options.B: Record the exact time on a chart
options.C: Ensure everyone is clear of the patient
options.D: Administer a dose of epinephrine

explanation: Always shout 'Clear!' and visually check that no one is touching the patient so the AED reads only their heart rhythm safely. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T6#GNS321_U2_T6_h5)

question: A nurse administrator checks a mobile medical unit. Which action best shows readiness for action?

options.A: Ordering excess supplies to fill every available inch of storage space
options.B: Relying entirely on local cellular networks for all emergency communication
options.C: Waiting until a disaster is officially declared before checking equipment
options.D: Verifying that supply carts and trauma kits match standardized inventory checklists

explanation: Using checklists ensures that every essential drug and piece of trauma gear is present and fully functional before deployment. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h3)

question: Why is immediate reporting of unusual disease symptoms by a PHC nurse critical?

options.A: It triggers a rapid public health response to prevent an outbreak
options.B: It allows the nurse to close the clinic early for the week
options.C: It fulfills a routine paperwork requirement without clinical impact
options.D: It secures financial bonuses for the local clinic staff

explanation: Quick reporting allows health authorities to investigate early and stop infectious diseases from spreading widely. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h5)

question: How does a hormonal IUD prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By thickening the cervical mucus to block sperm from entering
options.B: By making the vagina super acidic to destroy sperm on contact
options.C: By tricking the ovaries into releasing multiple eggs
options.D: By creating physical pressure that crushes any fertilized egg

explanation: The tiny bit of hormone released thickens the mucus at the cervix like a strong security guard—sperm just can't swim through it! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h2)

question: What is the most common cause of fever seen every day in Nigerian clinics?

options.A: Tuberculosis
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Meningitis
options.D: Malaria

explanation: Exactly right! Malaria is the leading cause of fever that nurses encounter across hospitals in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T6#GNS123_U3_T6_h3)

question: How should you position your patient's head during an eye wash?

options.A: Tilted slightly toward the affected side
options.B: Tilted firmly toward the unaffected side
options.C: Positioned flat and facing straight up
options.D: Tilted backward as far as the neck allows

explanation: Tilting toward the bad side ensures the dirty runoff flows away off the face instead of spilling into the healthy eye. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h4)

question: What safety advice should a nurse give a patient whose vision is slightly blurred from an anti-spasmodic?

options.A: Double the next dose to build up a drug tolerance
options.B: Avoid driving or operating machinery until vision clears
options.C: Stop taking all fluids immediately to reduce swelling
options.D: Rub the eyes vigorously with a warm damp cloth

explanation: Safety first! Blurry vision makes dangerous tasks like driving a real hazard until the medication wears off. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h7)

question: How does negative reinforcement keep a phobia going over time?

options.A: Taking medication increases the fear response every morning
options.B: Avoiding the feared object gives quick relief, making future avoidance more likely
options.C: Confronting the fear makes the anxiety disappear forever
options.D: Punishment from family members stops the patient from getting better

explanation: When you run away from what scares you, you feel instant relief. That brief relief rewards the escape behavior, making you more likely to run away again next time. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T6#GNS314_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a policy brief?

options.A: To display raw, unedited statistical calculations and formulas
options.B: To document the personal biography of the lead researcher
options.C: To provide concise, actionable recommendations for decision-makers
options.D: To serve as a textbook for first-year nursing students

explanation: Policy briefs summarize research for busy leaders so they can easily make informed decisions and rule changes. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why can spotting an adverse drug reaction sometimes be tricky for a nurse on the ward?

options.A: Patients refuse to talk about how they feel after taking drugs.
options.B: The symptoms often look like common illnesses or the original disease.
options.C: Laboratory tests always show normal values during a drug reaction.
options.D: ADRs only occur when the patient is discharged from the hospital.

explanation: It's easy to miss because signs like nausea, dizziness, or headache can easily be mistaken for the patient's actual sickness getting worse. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h3)

question: What is the job of the sticky adhesive pads that come with an AED?

question: What is the primary clinical definition of faecal incontinence?

question: Which sign helps you tell the difference between a simple blocked milk duct and acute mastitis?

question: How does the medication simethicone help relieve gas?

question: Which chemical messengers travel to the brain to raise body temperature and cause a fever during an infection?
